newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices fall, but a trade at last.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices fall, but a trade at last.

text.p: Asia's high sulphur fuel oil prices eased further on Wednesday but a deal was at last done -- at $93 per tonne -- after a three-week price slide, traders said.
A 20,000-tonne cargo loading February 17-23 fob Singapore was sold by British Petroleum (BP) to Dutch trader Vitol at $93 per tonne, down from the last deal done on December 30 of $124.
But, despite this, a major said "There is plenty of oil around."
A few enquiries were heard from Chinese buyers with bids at a premium of $5-$6 per tonne over spot quotes, for February deliveries. This was $3 below last week's levels.
Traders said freight costs to China have risen and were currently pegged at $9 per tonne. On a floating basis, premium in the fob Singapore market was assessed at par to 25 cents per tonne.
"This makes it very expensive to ship any Singapore supplies to southern China," a trader said.
South Korean supplies were heard offered at a discount to the Singapore spot quotes on a fob basis for January loading; February supplies were offered at flat to a slight 20 cents premia.
This compares with last week's premium of up to $1.00 per tonne fob South Korea.
A Japan refiner offered prompt fuel oil fob Japan at a $5.50 per tonne discount to Singapore spot quotes.
Traders said Fujairah supplies heard heading towards Singapore earlier in the week were already committed, traders said.
Rumours were also heard that a local trader would lift term supplies from Iran starting Thursday and may wish to see lower prices. The trader would not comment.
Optimistic sellers said prices may have reached a bottom and should be recovering. One trader said "crude and fuel oil spreads are too far apart."

Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) tender to sell high sulphur fuel oil was awarded to a Singapore trader, traders said. CPC sold the 30,000 tonne cargo for delivery February 18-27 at $101 a tonne, $30 off from its previous tender for Janaury deliveries.
In the swaps market, prices firmed in a technical correction from the recent price fall and on profit-taking.
